paper_metadata.title: Influence of Heat Treatment on Microstructure and Tensile Property of Ti-5Al-5Mo-5V-3Cr-1Fe Alloy

evidence.quote: Ti-5Al-5Mo-5V-3Cr-1Fe is a high strength beta alloy based on Timetal 555
having the following chemical composition (wt%): 5.23Al, 5.02Mo, 4.85V, 2.81Cr, 0.86Fe, 0.014C, 0.0010H, 0.101O, 0.018N, balanced Ti
Ti-5Al-5Mo-5V-3Cr-1Fe alloy was received from Baoji Titanium Industry Co., Ltd, China
The material ingot was produced by casting it twice in the consumable electrode vacuum furnace into a cylindrical mold of 150 mm in diameter
hot forged in the β phase field
then rolled into a billet 36mm in diameter in the (α+ β) phase field
followed by air cooling to room temperature
Solution heat treatment was carried out at various temperatures in (α+β) region as 800 ℃, 810 ℃and 820 ℃ for 1 h and air cooling
subsequent different aging temperature as 550 ℃ , 580 ℃ and 610 ℃ for 4 h
subsequent different aging temperature as 550 ℃ , 580 ℃ and 610 ℃ for 4 h
subsequent different aging temperature as 550 ℃ , 580 ℃ and 610 ℃ for 4 h

evidence.quote: After (α+ β) solution and aging treatment, the microstructure consists of primary α phase and transformed β phase with fine αs phase precipitating to improve the tensile strength effectively
As aging temperature increase, intragranular αs phase coarsening, resulting in lower strength but higher ductility
The plenty of dislocations can improve the tensile strength effectively
Ti-5Al-5Mo-5V-3Cr-1Fe is a high strength beta alloy based on Timetal 555
The material ingot was produced by casting it twice in the consumable electrode vacuum furnace into a cylindrical mold of 150 mm in diameter
hot forged in the β phase field
then rolled into a billet 36mm in diameter in the (α+ β) phase field
followed by air cooling to room temperature
all the microstructures consist of globular primary α phase (αp) and transformed β phase
These micrographs show the globular αp phase with the size about 5 µm
αs phase precipitates along grain boundaries and in the grain
Microstructure consists of αp phase and small beta subgrains in which αs phase precipitate
These micrographs show the globular αp phase with the size about 5 µm
The main dislocations are gathering around α phase grain boundary while few dislocations are scattered in α phase grains
After (α+ β) solution and aging treatment, the microstructure consists of primary α phase and transformed β phase with fine αs phase precipitating to improve the tensile strength effectively
As aging temperature increase, intragranular αs phase coarsening, resulting in lower strength but higher ductility
It is observed that increasing aging temperature can produce better ductility. That is certainly due to the coarsening of precipitated αs phase
The plenty of dislocations can improve the tensile strength effectively
